items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'Plot twist' gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. The quote 'One from ten leaves nought.' is delivered slowly and dryly, like a punchline. 'Twice.' lands as its own proud beat. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Say GTA as the letters G-T-A. Pronounce 'Caribbean' as 'kair-uh-BEE-un' and 'nought' as 'nawt'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word, every line in order; never add words of your own.
lines: What if the Caribbean... was one country?
Plot twist: part of it already was.
In nineteen fifty-eight, ten British island territories...
joined into one country: the West Indies Federation.
From Jamaica... all the way to Trinidad.
So what did this country get?
its own flag... and its own prime minister.
But here's the catch: Jamaica sat over eighteen hundred kilometers from the capital.
In nineteen sixty-one, Jamaica voted to leave.
Trinidad's leader did the math: One from ten leaves nought.
The country lasted just four years.
But that's not even the weirdest part.
They never really split up... in cricket.
Fifteen countries and territories still play as one team: the West Indies.
And they've won the World Cup. Twice.
And Jamaica has just one thing to say.
So... one Caribbean, or many? Because honestly...
